_comment: Ground v2 material manifest (2026-06-21 reset). Each entry packs into the texture arrays at its index. Rules drive PER-PIXEL placement (height m / slope 0-1) — NO baked splat. Biome = a manifest. tex_res = common array tiling resolution; tex_scale_m = world meters per texture tile. The 'placement' block holds the tunable knobs the shader reads as uniforms (promoted out of GLSL per the no-magic-numbers rule; key ones are also Debug-tab sliders).
_placement_doc: band_soft_m=height-band edge softness (m); slope_soft=slope-band softness (0-1); warp_m=domain-warp wavelength (m); warp_amp_m=domain-warp amplitude (m); patch_m=within-area variation patch wavelength (m); noise_gain=how strongly patch noise modulates each weight; height_bias=Unit-4 strength real height biases the boundary.
_height_range_note: Bands fit the lab field's actual elevation (~ -180..639 m). Retune per biome/terrain; the field range is printed at startup as 'TerrainLab: built ... (h MIN..MAX m)'.
_coverage_note: Bands must TILE the (height x slope) space — if some (h,slope) is in no material's band, placement falls back to material index 0 (clay). DESIGN: flat materials stack by height (clay->sand->...->powder, slope<~0.45); slope materials stack by height (scree->talus, ~0.28..0.6); basalt is the STEEPEST-face cliff (slope>=0.6, any height); lichen is high non-cliff slope. Keep overlap small so each (h,slope) has ONE clear winner + at most one neighbor — heavy overlap = a chaotic patchwork.
